articles.headline: The PNP opens a nationwide hunt as Bato dela Rosa's surrender week ends
articles.descriptionHtml: The one-week surrender window Interior Secretary Jonvic Remulla set last Friday closed on October 30 without Senator Ronald "Bato" dela Rosa turning himself in; Lt. Gen. Wilson Joseph Lopez said Immigration records still put him in the country, no surrender feelers had arrived, and tracker teams now sit in every region. The same week in The Hague, prosecutors asked to admit recorded testimonies that mention dela Rosa and drug-war target lists, victims' lawyers backed three of those statements, the ICC Registry forwarded 46 applications covering 96 people classed as clearly qualifying victims, and Rodrigo Duterte waived his appearance at the November 2 status conference. Last week's bounty is now a nationwide hunt, while the November 30 trial is lining up victim evidence.

articles.headline: The Supreme Court tells Congress to comment on the lowered conviction-vote rule
articles.descriptionHtml: The Supreme Court on October 29 made public an October 14 order giving the Senate impeachment court and the House five days to comment on the Padilla–Go petition against the Senate's lowered conviction-vote rule — the threshold fight last week's coverage only flagged as coming. House spokesman Zia Alonto Adiong said ₱463,046,459 in alleged unexplained wealth remains even after corporate assets are stripped from Alexander Cabrera's ₱817.87-million estimate, a figure the Senate court has not adopted. A man using the alias "Chris," who said he drove for former Speaker Lord Allan Velasco, told the NBI on October 29 he ferried suitcases to Davao in 2021–22 but never saw the contents or the Vice President; both camps called him a planted witness. The defense opens November 9 with both the math of conviction and the remaining peso figure still unsettled.

articles.headline: Watchdogs flag a ₱4.38-billion DPWH jump for Sandro Marcos's district
articles.descriptionHtml: What changed from last week's Supreme Court spending ceiling is a named district: watchdogs told the Senate on October 26 that Ilocos Norte's 1st — House Majority Leader Sandro Marcos's — took the largest House insertion, ₱4.375 billion on the People's Budget Coalition count and ₱4.38 billion above the ₱369-million presidential proposal on BetterGov.ph's DPWH tally, a mapping they said does not prove he requested the projects. Senate President Sherwin Gatchalian had already pledged to strip lump-sum funds from the ₱7.2-trillion bill; the coalition put more than ₱1 trillion in red flags, including nearly 7,000 House-added projects worth ₱190 billion with no published attachments. The president's son's district now sits at the top of the insertion list the Senate says it will cut.

articles.headline: Bernardo tells the Sandiganbayan Jinggoy Estrada took ₱573 million in kickbacks
articles.descriptionHtml: State witness Roberto Bernardo told the Sandiganbayan on October 28 that detained Senator Jinggoy Estrada received ₱573 million in infrastructure "commitments" in four tranches from November 2024 to June 2025, hauled from the Diamond Hotel to San Juan — a peso figure last week's flood-control coverage did not yet have. He also said former senators Nancy Binay and Grace Poe were allotted 12–15% and 20% kickbacks; Estrada called the account inconsistent and denied any cash. The same cluster had DPWH engineer Carlo Rivera saying Martin Romualdez was not on the proponent list for the ₱5-billion Co deliveries, and on October 30 the Ombudsman preventively suspended five Bulacan First District engineers over ₱188.9 million in Baliuag flood-control projects. The plunder cases now name a sitting senator's peso trail, not only a speaker-adjacent omission.

articles.headline: The peso breaks ₱64 as Marcos tells the public not to panic
articles.descriptionHtml: The peso closed at ₱64.17 per dollar on October 27 — the first finish through ₱64, 22 centavos past Monday's ₱63.95 record — after an intraday low of ₱64.20. President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. told reporters the next day not to panic, blamed oil and fuel, and said the government would "defend the peso as hard as we possibly can" with healthy reserves; the unit then recovered to ₱64.025. A weaker peso raises the import bill for fuel and food that OFW families and households at home both feel.

articles.headline: ASEAN defense ministers meet in Cebu as the US adds funds and Teodoro snubs China
articles.descriptionHtml: The week the Armed Forces counted 54 Chinese navy and coast guard ships in the West Philippine Sea from October 20–26 — up from 31 — ASEAN defense ministers met in Cebu. On the sidelines, US War Secretary Pete Hegseth announced more security-cooperation funds for AFP modernization without naming an amount, and Defense Secretary Gilberto Teodoro Jr. and Japan's Shinjiro Koizumi agreed to move the first retired Abukuma-class warship as soon as it is decommissioned. Teodoro did not personally receive China's defense attaché, Senior Captain Yang Lei, and rejected Beijing's claim that Manila had abused its chairmanship; China had sent its lowest-level ADMM-Plus delegation since 2010. Manila stacked US money and a Japanese hull in the same week the WPS ship count nearly doubled and Beijing walked the meeting down to an attaché.

articles.headline: Hunt.io finds 68 GB of backups matching DMW and POEA systems
articles.descriptionHtml: Hunt.io reported on October 28 that an operator copied 27 SQL Server backups totaling 68.837 GiB on September 6, with filenames matching POEA, OFW, and Balik-Manggagawa systems now under the Department of Migrant Workers; the National Privacy Commission said on October 29 it is investigating possible Data Privacy Act violations and coordinating with the DMW. The researchers did not examine the backups, and they have not established that personal information was accessed or where the files went. OFW case-management systems are in the filenames, but a leak of worker data has not been confirmed.
